second_order: building, correcting, and maintaining the taskbar
theme_note: These passages do the manual work of making, correcting, finishing, or maintaining the Start button and taskbar; what varies is whether the work begins a feature, fixes a pixel-level defect, or keeps an existing part usable.

These passages align builders by publishing templates, grids, layouts, dimensions, colours, spacing, and refresh instructions; what varies is the plan's version and the part of the taskbar it governs.

second_order: using scripts and bots to place and maintain pixels
theme_note: These passages use or contest scripts, bots, and unusually rapid placement as ways of extending or maintaining pixels; what varies is whether automation is offered as help, blamed for damage, or criticized as unfair.

second_order: recruiting people and focusing their work
theme_note: These passages recruit labour and direct attention toward a shared job; what varies is whether people are asked to join, defend, repair, finish, or concentrate on one location.

second_order: moving coordination and negotiation to Discord
theme_note: These passages move coordination, diplomacy, or viewing away from the Reddit thread into Discord or another live venue; what varies is whether people seek access, publish an invite, report a broken link, or bring a decision back.

second_order: asking the taskbar to stop or spare existing art
theme_note: These passages ask the advancing taskbar to stop, go around, or leave existing work intact; what varies is whether the appeal sets an endpoint, names labour already invested, or accepts a border while refusing erasure.

second_order: fitting threatened art into windows, tabs, and icons
theme_note: These passages handle collisions by moving or remaking threatened work as a window, tab, icon, tray item, border, or shifted piece; what varies is who requests accommodation and which Windows object is offered.

second_order: making treaties and trading help across borders
theme_note: These passages make or dispute treaties, borders, reciprocal help, and representative agreements; what varies is the parties, the promised exchange, and whether speakers accept the authority of the deal.

These passages propose new Windows-flavoured objects, jokes, controls, applications, and visual details for the shared design; what varies is the object proposed and whether it is nostalgic, functional, or playful.

second_order: pressing the taskbar onward and claiming room
theme_note: These passages make continued growth and completion the priority, claiming more of the bottom or urging a march toward the clock; what varies is whether expansion is justified by manpower, maintainability, or the project's stated end goal.

second_order: mocking, condemning, and resisting the taskbar
theme_note: These passages oppose the project by condemning, mocking, threatening, or withdrawing support from its expansion; what varies is whether resistance is moral criticism, parody, insult, or organized counter-action.

second_order: celebrating, thanking, and recounting the work
theme_note: These passages praise, thank, welcome, and recount what participants built together; what varies is whether they mark the Start button, community growth, an accommodation, the end of Place, or the final image.

second_order: checking what is happening and what remains to do
theme_note: These passages check the project's status, responsibilities, unresolved questions, and visible results; what varies is whether the speaker asks what happened, reports a limit, or assesses what remains unsettled.

second_order: defending and repairing the taskbar and incorporated art
theme_note: These passages respond to attacks or damage by warning, repairing, maintaining, or calling defenders; what varies is the threatened object and whether the danger is described as void, griefing, corruption, or an attack.

second_order: calling to remove or replace other work
theme_note: These passages call for another work to be removed, replaced, or yielded to a stronger project; what varies is the target and whether the call is blunt destruction or displacement framed as inevitable.

second_order: playing with Windows and taskbar jokes
theme_note: These passages play with Windows, taskbar, and subreddit language for amusement rather than issuing an operational plan; what varies is the pun or parody used.

second_order: ending Place and restarting on another canvas
theme_note: These passages answer the end of placement by proposing another canvas or another run of the Windows bar; what varies is the replacement venue and whether continuation is announced, invited, or merely proposed.
